FOREWORD

Indian Standard was -adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 December 1983, after the draft finalized by the Fish and Fisheries Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. standard has been consumer interest and helping control of the product. formulated with a view to safeguarding the processors in exercising proper quality

0.2This

0.3 In the preparation of this standard due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in The number of significant places accordance with IS : Z-1960*. retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

2. GRADES 2.1 The tuna shall be of the following Grade Designation Large Small 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 General 3.1.1 The tuna shall be of good quality and free from any evidence of The material to be canned shall be free from degradation and spoilage. heads, bones, skin, tail trps, fins and entrails and shall be free from any The skin shall not be taint suggestives of the defective raw material. dark in colour and shall be free from discoloration. 3.1.2 Fat - Only pure, wholesome refined edible fat shall be used for cooking, the percentage of fat in the total contents of a can shall be less than 4 percent by volume. 3.1.3 Salt - Salt of edible quality preferably conforming to IS : 5941962" shall be used. The percentage of salt in the final product shall not be less than 1 percent and not more than 2 percent. 3.1.4 Other Ingredients - Spices and all other ingredients used shall be clean, sound and wholesome and fit for human consumption and shall conform to relevant Indian Standard, if available. 3.2 Freedom from Artificial Colouring Matter and Firming Agents - The material shall be free from artificial colouring matter and firming agents except common salt. *Specification for common :alt for fish curing ( revised). 4 two grades: Mass, Whole, g above 1 000

up to 1 000

IS : 10762 - 1983 3.3 Additives -be used. No additives other than spices and common salt shall

as agreed to 3.4 Preparation - The fish curry shall be prepared between the purchaser and the packer, care being taken that during preparation all the meat juices or other ingredients are retained in full, Any of the appropriate permitted spices and processing. during condiments may be used. 3.4.1 Processing - Processing shall be at such a temperature, and for such length of time as will ensure thorough cooking and adequate sterilization of the finished product. The water used for the cooling of can shall be maintained in clean condition and chlorinated to maintain a minimum free residual chlorine concentration of one rug/kg ( ppm ). 3.5 Hygienic and processed Requirements - The material shall be prepared, filled under hygienic conditions and only in premises maintained in a thoroughly clean and hygienic manner [ see IS : 4303 ( part 2 )1975* ] and duly approved or licensed by the authorities concerned for fish products. The water used for processing of fish shall conform to IS : 4251-1967t. 3.5.1

shall

quality

3.6

Packing

3.6.1 The material shall be packed in suitable containers and hermetically sealed. If the cans are lacquered, the lacquer used shall be nontoxic and shall be of such quality that it does not impart any foreign taste and smell to the contents of the can and does not peel off during The lacquer shall be not soluble processing and storage of the product. in oil or brine to any extent: The can shall be free from rust. The cans shall be thoroughly cleaned before filling. 3.6.2 remain 3.6.3 3.7 The tuna shall be filled in the cans in such a manner in the same axis, that is, there shall be no crossfilling. 4.1 Packing - Unless agreed to otherwise between the purchaser and the vendor, the cans shall be packed in cases sufficiently strong to withstand rough handling by all modes of transportation without damage to their contents. - The labelling of the cans shall be done either by 4.2 Marking printing or lithographing on the cans themselves~or by attaching labels printed on paper, subject to agreement between the purchaser and the vendor. 4.2.1 Each container shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the following information in addition to information required under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and rules: a) Name of the material along with brand name, if any; ( optional -for export ); ~b) Name and address of the manufacturer c) Net mass of the contents of the can; d) Proportion of fish curry in the cans, if required by the purchaser; e) Nature ~of the canning medium used and ingredients; f> Licence number, date and authority, if any, under which the manufacturer has been permitted to can the product ( optional for export ); d Batch or lot number and the date of manufacture; and

APPENDIX ( Clause 3.7.6 )
DETERMINATION

A

OF THE PROPORTION GRAVY

OF FISH

TO

A-l.

APPARATUS 2*80-mm IS Sieve - BS Sieve 7, ASTM Sieve 7 and Tyler Sieve their apertures within the limits specified for the IS Sieve and therefore, be used as 2.80 mm IS Sieve [ see IS : 460 ( Part 1 )1. 16-mm IS Sieve

A-l.1 7 have may, 19787 A-l.2

A-2. PROCEDURE
A-2.1 Record the mass of the containter, warm the contents of the can containing fish. Open the container and drain over 16-mm IS Sieve. Wash the empty container with hot water and pour it over the fish. Dry and weigh the empty container. Pour hot water over the fish three or four times to remove all adhering condiments and fat. Ensure that the fish are free from all adhering matters; if necessary, repeat washing with hot water. Allow the fish to be completely drained of water. Place the fish in the empty container and weigh. Calculate the proportion of fish to gravy. A-2.2 When determining the proportion of fish content to gravy, IS Sieve shall be used. The gravy should be ground to a fine as to pass through the sieve.

B-3.1 Vacuum and Visual Examination - Each of the cans selected from the lot according to B-2.3 shall be first tested for vacuum 3.7.5 and then examined for visual requirements given in 3.7.1, 3.7.3 and 3.7.4. B-3.1.1 The lot shall be declared as conforming to these requirements if none of the sample cans fails +o satisfy any of these requirements. B-3.2 Drained Mass ( 3.7.6 ) Disintegrated Units ( 3.7.2 ) - The lot having been found satisfactory according to B-3.1 shall be tested for these requirements. B-3.2.1 The lot shall be deemed to have met the requirements for drained mass and disintegrated units if the average of the test results for 5 cans satisfies the relevant specification requirements.
NOTE - Whenever there are nlore than 5 cans, they shall be randomly into groups qf 5 cans each. distributed

B-3.3 Metallic Impurities - The lot having met the requirements in B-3.1 and B-3-2 shall be tested for arsenic, lead, copper, zinc, tin and mercury according to 3.7.7 of the specification on the basis of a composite sample prepared by mjxmg approximately equal quantity of the material from all the cans sampled from a lot. B-3.3.1 The lot shall be declared as conforming to these requirements ifall the test results on the composite sample meet the relevant specification requirements given in Table 1 of the specification. B-3.4 Microbiological Activity - The factory according to B-3.1, B-3.2 and B-3.3 microbiological activity according to 3.7.7. lot havil;lg been found satisshall be finally tested for
